title: The Flipping Game

concept.title: A position is winning if some move leads to a losing position
body: A string of `+` and `-` is the board. In one move a player picks **two neighbouring** `+` and turns both into `-`. The players alternate, and a player who has **no move** loses. For games like this there is a simple recursive rule: a position is **winning** for the player to move if at least one move leads to a position that is **losing** for the opponent. A position without moves is losing.

Different move orders reach the same board (`++++` after the first and the last flip is `--++` + ... and so on), so the results are stored in a dictionary keyed by the board. The loop stops at the first winning move, because one is enough. A position with no `++` has an empty loop, so `result` stays `False`: it is lost.

statement: A board is a string of `+` and `-`. In one move a player chooses two neighbouring `+` characters and changes both into `-`. The two players move in turn, the first player starts, and a player who cannot move loses. Both play perfectly. Print `yes` if the first player wins and `no` otherwise.
inputFormat: The only line has the board.

examples.note: The first player flips the middle two characters (+--+). Now the second player has no move and loses.

hints: A position without two neighbouring plus signs is lost for the player to move.
A position is won if some move gives a lost position to the opponent.
Store the result for each board text: the same board appears again and again.

explanation: A board is winning when some flip leaves the opponent a losing board; a board with no `++` is losing. A dictionary keyed by the board text makes each board cost one scan.
solution.complexity: Time O(number of reachable boards * n), space the same.
